headline: South Asia: Makkah defence pact meeting to be held today in Riyadh, confirms FO
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Makkah defence pact meeting to be held today in Riyadh, confirms FO.
- Western Russia: Three killed and 35 injured, including children, in at least three Russian guided bomb strikes on Kharkiv – video.
- Africa: Sudan: Sudan Doctors Network - Four Civilians Killed in RSF Drone Attacks On South Kordofan.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: ‘UNINFORMED’ - Global Afrikan Congress rebukes Warmington over slave trade remarks, urges him to do research and apologise.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: ‘UNINFORMED’ - Global Afrikan Congress rebukes Warmington over slave trade remarks, urges him to do research and apologise.
The Global Afrikan Congress (GAC) is demanding an apology from parliamentarian Everald Warmington for his “uninformed assertions” that Black Africans who sold people into the transatlantic slave trade should be held more accountable than Europeans buyers. In an open letter to Warmington, the GAC – an international Pan-African organisation of people of African descent across 35 countries – also urged the St Catherine South Western member of parliament (MP) to undertake necessary research to correct his “colonial miseducation”.
United States: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Three killed and 35 injured, including children, in at least three Russian guided bomb strikes on Kharkiv – video.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Three killed and 35 injured, including children, in at least three Russian guided bomb strikes on Kharkiv – video.
Russian forces attacked the city of Kharkiv with at least three guided aerial bombs and a combat drone on 5 October, killing three people and leaving 35 others in need of medical treatment, including children.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Officers involved in strikes on Ukraine were among eight killed in Tu-95MS crash in Russia.
Eight military personnel, including at least three officers linked to combat missions or their preparation by the Ukrainian project Book of Executioners, were killed when a Russian Tu-95MS strategic bomber crashed in Amur Oblast on 29 September.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Ukrainian forces strike Russian drone launch site, control point and drone warehouse – General Staff.
Ukraine's General Staff reported targeted strikes on Russian drone launch sites, command posts and UAV warehouses in Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia oblasts.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Russian drones attack Turkish vessel, captain killed – Zelenskyy.
Zelenskyy says two Russian drones hit a Turkish-owned civilian vessel carrying maize in neutral waters, killing its captain.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Kosovo Parliament Moves Towards Changing Law to Curb Hague Special Court.
- Balkan Insight, one hour ago: Kosovo Parliament Moves Towards Changing Law to Curb Hague Special Court.
MPs in first reading adopt major changes to law governing the Hague-based war crimes court following conviction of former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders – although enforcement requires second vote.
- Politico Europe, Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Germany risks being drawn into ‘violent conflict’ with Russia, spy chief warns.
The head of Germany’s foreign intelligence agency also cautioned that NATO countries must beware of Moscow's "little green men."
- Politico Europe, 3 hours ago: Suspected plague in Russia puts EU on alert.
“We are aware of the reports concerning the laboratory incident in Russia, seemingly involving a pathogen-causing plague,” says European Commission spokesperson.
- Politico Europe, 7 hours ago: Is Kemi Badenoch abandoning the Red Wall?.
Is Andy Burnham an easier opponent for the Conservatives than Sir Keir Starmer? At the Tory conference in Birmingham, Kemi Badenoch’s team sniff a chance to attack the prime minister – with a particular chance to seize on and attack his economic argument. Sam Coates and Anne McElvoy pore over Badenoch’s “The Right Way” pamphlet […]

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Sudan: Sudan Doctors Network - Four Civilians Killed in RSF Drone Attacks On South Kordofan.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 4 hours ago: Sudan: Sudan Doctors Network - Four Civilians Killed in RSF Drone Attacks On South Kordofan.
[Dabanga] Dilling, South Kordofan -- Four civilians, including a child and a woman, have been killed in RSF drone strikes on residential neighbourhoods in Dilling, South Kordofan, the Sudan Doctors Network says. The network condemns the attacks as a grave violation of international humanitarian law.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 9 hours ago: Sudan: Sudan War - Fighting On Ethiopian Border, Drone Attacks On Ed Damazin.
[Dabanga] Ed Damazin -- The RSF-aligned Tasees Alliance forces announced on Saturday that they had taken full control of areas in Roseires locality, north-east of Ed Damazin, capital of Sudan's Blue Nile state, after seizing several areas, including Menze, Jabal El Nimr, Jabal El Num, Basharkat, Matanguya, Mangaling El Jawani, Masnabiga, and Makala.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 22 hours ago: Sudan: 'Drone Strike On El Obeid Shelter Kills Boy, Wounds 12 Children'.
[Dabanga] El Obeid -- A drone strike on a shelter for internally displaced people in El Obeid, North Kordofan, late on Thursday reportedly killed a boy and wounded 12 children, as another drone strike on a university dormitory in the city killed five civilians and injured 47 others.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 9 hours ago: Ethiopia: Ethiopia's New Rebel War Redraws Alliances Across the Horn of Africa.
[RFI] Ethiopia and Eritrea have cut diplomatic ties as a new rebel offensive grips northern Ethiopia, putting two countries that fought together during the last Tigray war on opposing sides. Ethiopia accuses its neighbour of supporting a new anti-government alliance.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Israel is world's second-most targeted country by cyberattacks, Microsoft finds.
- Jerusalem Post, one hour ago: Israel is world's second-most targeted country by cyberattacks, Microsoft finds.
"In cyberspace, you may not see missiles in the air, but there is no ceasefire," said head of the National Cyber Directorate, Yossi Karadi, in response to the report.
- Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: IDF killed two-thirds of terrorists who invaded Israel on October 7, intel chief tells cabinet.
"There are 2,000 remaining, and we will get to every last one of them," Maj.-Gen. Shlomi Binder, head of the IDF's Military Intelligence, told the security cabinet on Sunday evening.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: Yemen war: What’s the latest, as government forces claim advances?.
After launching major military offensive to reclaim Houthi-held areas, Yemeni government says it has taken key district.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Iran executes two men arrested over January 2026 protests, Mizan reports.
Mizan said Alireza Sepahi and Alireza Raeisi were sentenced to death on charges including "membership in an armed rebel group, and waging war against God through carrying weapons."
South Africa: no notable developments in the last 24 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Makkah defence pact meeting to be held today in Riyadh, confirms FO.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: Makkah defence pact meeting to be held today in Riyadh, confirms FO.
A meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement will be held on Monday in Riyadh and will focus on regional developments and ongoing cooperation among the member states, the Foreign Office (FO) confirmed. In a statement on social media platform X, the FO said Pakistan’s delegation to the meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) will include Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 14 hours ago: Haunted by grief, Gaza’s displaced still wait overseas for return.
CAIRO: Omar al-Hassayna fled Gaza for Cairo after an Israeli airstrike wiped out much of his large family. Three years on, he remains there waiting for enough stability, security and reconstruction in his still devastated homeland to return. Hassayna is one of more than 100,000 Gazans who left the enclave during the war and remain stranded overseas, according to Palestinian Authority figures. They still mourn dead relatives and their destroyed homes and neighbourhoods.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: Only ‘just, fair’ talks can end war, Iran tells US.
TEHRAN: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared on Sunday that there was no military solution to the US’ war against the Islamic Republic and that only negotiations based on “justice and fairness” could end the conflict, as talks between Washington and Tehran appeared to be at an impasse. “If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force,” Araghchi told a gathering of foreign ambassadors in Tehran.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: ‘Abandoned province’: Amir Muqam slams PTI, says not in favour of governor’s rule in KP but security risks persist.
Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam on Monday slammed the PTI-led government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, stressing that the federal government was not “in favour of governor’s rule” amid the party’s march, but warning of national security risks. The minister’s comments came as KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi launched the party’s long march towards Islamabad on Sunday, saying that the party would “not accept” any policy against the interests of the people of KP. PTI went ahead with its march despite warnings from the federal government.
India - bottom line: 'Intend To Complete Missions': Netanyahu Vows No Hamas Rule In Gaza.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: 'Intend To Complete Missions': Netanyahu Vows No Hamas Rule In Gaza.
Since Hamas's October 2023 attack, Israel has fought wars on several fronts, including against Iran-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Beyond the F-35: US, China are racing to build 6th-gen jets that will command drone fleets.
Sixth-generation fighter aircraft are expected to revolutionize air warfare by incorporating advanced technologies and strong connectivity. Both the US and China are at the forefront of developing these advanced military systems. Collaborations among nations like the UK, Japan, and Italy aim to create powerful multirole aircraft. The shift to network-centric warfare emphasizes the importance of information dominance in future conflicts. As these advancements unfold, traditional combat approaches may evolve significantly.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Why did AJ Styles return to the ring 246 days after WWE retirement?.
AJ Styles made a surprising return to the wrestling ring to assist his son, Avery, during a match. Avery was attacked by allies of his opponent, Tristan Moody, after winning by disqualification. Styles, who had recently retired, rushed in to help Avery and fought off the attackers. The emotional moment between father and son highlighted the bond they share as wrestling becomes a family affair.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: No Hardeep Puri, Smriti Irani: The New BJP Faces For UP Rajya Sabha Polls.
Dharam Pal Singh, Radhakant Ojha, Prakash Pal, Vidyasagar Sonkar, Gopi Krishna Pandey, Priyanka Singh Rawat, Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan and Shruti Gangwar are the eight BJP candidates for the Rajya Sabha polls.

South Korea ⁠said on Monday that a ⁠recent border blast that seriously wounded two ⁠of its soldiers was caused by mines planted by North Korea. North Korea, which has been fortifying its border with South Korea since April 2024, deployed up to 7,000 workers to install mines and fences this year, with some 50 incidents of ‌crossing the border, according to a briefing on Monday by the South’s military. Built to hunt tanks and support ground troops, the People’s Liberation Army’s main attack helicopter is increasingly being prepared for operations at sea. Crews of the Z-10 are training to fly from ships – a shift that could give Beijing extra firepower in an amphibious assault on Taiwan. Manufactured by AVIC subsidiary the Changhe Aircraft Industries Corporation, the Z-10 entered service with the PLA Army in late 2010. - South China Morning Post - China, 10 hours ago: India seeks to be ‘a little bit more involved’ in ending Ukraine war: minister.
India is taking a more direct role in efforts to end the conflict between Russia and Ukraine, engaging both sides on issues including shipping and reducing hostilities, Minister of External Affairs S. Jaishankar has said. Speaking at a security conference over the weekend, Jaishankar said India in recent months has become “a little bit more involved beyond advocacy”. AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Australian leaders condemn pro-Palestine vigils planned for 7 October anniversary amid Jewish commemorations.
- The Guardian - Australia, just now: Australian leaders condemn pro-Palestine vigils planned for 7 October anniversary amid Jewish commemorations.
Peak Jewish bodies organise ceremonies on third anniversary of attacks that triggered conflict in which 74,000 Palestinians have been killed Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Jewish Australians will mark the third anniversary of the 7 October attacks on Wednesday as Labor state governments condemn pro-Palestinian vigils to be held the same day. Peak Jewish bodies have organised commemorations across the capital cities but avoided publicising locations as community members report ongoing fears for their safety since the Bondi terror attack in December.
